{{External|os=Skilling success rate}} The '''skilling success function''' (often called '''stat_random''') is used to determine whether or not a skilling action is successful, granting the player with rewards (generally items and experience). The formula approximates linear interpolation. As the player's level in a skill increases, the chance of success generally increases too. The function calculates a value which is compared to a random number to determine that action's success. ==Mechanics== Each action that uses the skilling success function uses two parameters in addition to the player's level: a 'high' value and a 'low' value. The high value represents the odds that the action is successful at level 99, and the low value at level 1 (regardless of the actual level requirement of the action). The values for levels between (and after) are calculated using this interpolation formula: :\text{interpolate}(level) = low + \left\lfloor\frac{(high-low) \times (level-1)}{98}\right\rfloor The value is then scaled up by 10,000, then any boosts are applied (see below). The resulting value is then compared to a random number that is generated from 0 to 2550000, effectively meaning the value can be taken as a chance out of 2550001 of success. :\text{stat}\_\text{random}(level) = \frac{\left\lfloor 10000 \times \text{interpolate}(level) \times boosts \right\rfloor}{2550001} Due to the integer calculation of the game's engine (represented with a floor function above), the success chance doesn't always increase; it often remains the same for several consecutive levels. {{Skilling success chart|skill=fishing|label=Monkfish fishing chance|showbefore=no|label1=Raw monkfish|image1=Raw monkfish.png|low1=48|high1=90|req1=62}} Unlike [[osrsw:Skilling success rate|skilling success in Old School RuneScape]], the level input is not clamped to 99; this allows skills that can be levelled above 99 (e.g. [[Archaeology]]) to function to level 120, and boosts above level 99 (or 120) also have an effect. Additionally, after the [[2024 Woodcutting, Fletching, and Firemaking update]] which added 110 Woodcutting, the high and low values for success chance calulation were scaled up (that is, before interpolation), so the interpolation is generally smoother. ===Calculator=== {| class="wikitable" ! colspan="2" | Low chance ! colspan="2" | High chance ! colspan="2" | Level |- | colspan="2" class="jcInput" |name=lowchance|type=int|value=0|sublist=calcchance | colspan="2" class="jcInput" |name=highchance|type=int|value=256|sublist=calcchance | colspan="2" class="jcInput" |name=levelinp|type=int|value=1|range=1,200|sublist=calcchance |- ! colspan="3" | Interpolated value ! colspan="3" | Chance |- | colspan="3" class="jcInput" |name=interp|type=output|value=- | colspan="3" class="jcInput" |name=percchance|type=output|value=- |}
calcchance| let(x1, highchance-lowchance) let(x2, levelinp-1) let(x3, x1*x2) let(x3, x3/98) let(x3, floor(x3)) let(interp, x3+lowchance) let(x4, interp / 255.0001) let(x4, x4 * 100000) let(x4, floor(x4)) let(x4, x4/1000) let(percchance, x4 + "%")
==Cascading chances== Some activities, particularly in [[Fishing]], have multiple possible rewards, which follows a cascading format. Generally this means the highest level reward is rolled for first, and then if that is unsuccessful the next reward is rolled for, and so on; if all possible reward rolls fail, nothing is awarded. For example, a player using the [[barbarian rod]] with 85 [[Fishing]] as well as the other requirements to catch a [[leaping sturgeon]] first rolls against the skilling success formula for leaping sturgeon. Since leaping sturgeon have a low value of 8 and a high value of 64, the chance of getting a leaping sturgeon is (in these examples we are using 1/255.0001 instead of 10000/2550001 for simplicity) : P_{\text{sturgeon}}(85) = \dfrac{8 + \left\lfloor\dfrac{(64 - 8) \times (85 - 1)}{98}\right\rfloor}{255.0001} = \dfrac{8 + \left\lfloor\dfrac{56 \times 84}{98}\right\rfloor}{255.0001} = \dfrac{8 + 48}{255.0001} = 0.21961 If the player fails to get a leaping sturgeon, a [[leaping salmon]] is rolled for. Since leaping salmon have a low value of 16 and a high value of 96, the '''chance of getting a leaping salmon given that the player failed the leaping sturgeon roll''' is : P_{\text{salmon}}(85) = \dfrac{16 + \left\lfloor\dfrac{(96-16) \times (85 - 1)}{98}\right\rfloor}{255.0001} = \dfrac{16 + \left\lfloor\dfrac{80 \times 84}{98}\right\rfloor}{255.0001} = \dfrac{16+68}{255.0001} = 0.32941 So the chance of failing to catch a sturgeon and instead catching a leaping salmon at level 85 is : (1-P_{\text{sturgeon}}(85)) \times P_{\text{salmon}}(85) = (1-0.21961) \times 0.32941 \approx 0.25707 Similarly, the chance that a player fails to catch both a leaping sturgeon and leaping salmon, but catches a leaping trout, which has a low value of 32 and a high value of 192, is : (1-P_{\text{sturgeon}}(85)) \times (1-P_{\text{salmon}}(85)) \times P_{\text{trout}}(85) \approx 0.34683 If the all three rolls are failed, the player receives nothing. Thus, in this example, with 10,000 attempts, a player can expect: * 2196 leaping sturgeon * 2571 leaping salmon * 3468 leaping trout * 1765 nothing ==Boosts== * Visible level boosts - e.g. potions - simply increase the level input for the interpolation function. * Some boosts apply before the interpolation function, by modifying the values of high and low. As these usually apply to relatively smally numbers, these are often subject to integer rounding. Some examples of these include: ** [[Honed]] perk ** Several [[familiar]]s with 'invisible level' boosts ** [[Lockpick]]s used on pre-[[120 Thieving update]] chests and doors * Some boosts apply after the interpolation function, by scaling the interpolated value. This is after the chance is multiplied by 10,000, so integer rounding is negligible. These are: ** [[Five finger discount]] upgrade ** [[Skillchompa]]s (Fishing, Archaeology) ** [[Ring of whispers]] (Fishing, Woodcutting, Hunter, Archaeology) ** [[Fury shark outfit|Fury shark]], [[Nature's sentinel outfit|nature's sentinel]], [[Volcanic trapper outfit|Volcanic trapper]], and the lesser variants ** [[Master archaeologist's outfit]]s ** [[Crystal rod]] and [[Tavia's rod]] ** [[Perfect juju fishing potion]] ** [[Sana's fyrtorch]] ** [[Crystal Mask]] ** [[Soul-in-a-box]] ** [[Gloves of silence]]/[[Exoskeleton bracers]] ** [[Ardougne achievements]] pickpocketing buff ** [[Ring of Vitur]] ** [[Magpie]] familiar ** [[Dundee's Crocodile Upgrades|Increased Whirligig catch chance]] ==Usages== The skilling success function is used widely by many skills, including: * [[Fishing]] * [[Woodcutting]] * [[Agility]] * [[Archaeology]] * [[Thieving]] * Pre-[[Mining and Smithing rework|rework]] [[Mining]] ==Update history== {{UH| * {{UL|update=Player Owned Farm|date=3 September 2018}} ** The addition of extreme skilling potions brought a rewrite of the skilling success function to: *** Slightly improve success chances across the board (effectively every chance +1) *** Allow levels above 99 to have an effect }} {{mechanics}}
